note: Required user-facing notices that the native iOS core renders inline, and which therefore cannot be held in the web sources the path-scoped compliance guards read (ADR 0018 D9). Each entry names the web source that must carry the SAME wording: scripts/check-native-copy.mjs asserts the text is present there verbatim (whitespace- and markup-normalised) and that apps/mobile/ios/App/App/Generated/LegalCopy.swift is the exact rendering of this file. Web-side rewording therefore fails the build until this register and the generated Swift are updated together, so the two channels cannot state different things. Copy that is modal- or print-shaped is NOT registered here: it stays in the WebView islands (D8) where it needs no second rendering.

entries.note: Opens the ballot acknowledgement on the card, live and archived alike.

entries.text: How2Vote does not recommend a candidate or a preference order
entries.note: The DISC-NO-RECOMMENDATION disclaimer itself (docs/legal/required-checks.json). Registered without terminal punctuation because the live and archived notices continue the sentence differently.

entries.text: A voting plan is not a ballot paper: copy your numbers onto the official paper at the polling place and follow the AEC's instructions.
entries.note: Distinguishes the plan from an official ballot paper on the live card.

entries.text: Preference order selected by the user.
entries.note: Already a single-sourced constant on the web (PREFERENCE_SOURCE_NOTICE); registered so the native rendering is bound to the same string.

entries.text: You chose every number — How2Vote does not recommend a candidate or a preference order.
entries.note: The plan foot's user-authorship statement, which carries the s321D authoriser model (ADR 0010).

Announced as part of a link's accessible name before it is followed (WCAG 3.2.5), so a screen-reader user is not dropped into an unexplained context. The wording is channel-specific: the shells open an in-app browser rather than a new tab, and link-conventions.test.ts already holds the web to this on its side.

entries.text: Tap a question to change your answer. Star (★) the issues that matter most — only your strongest answers can count ten times as much.
entries.note: States how the ×10 importance lever works and, in the same breath, its limit — that it attaches only to the strongest answers. A native review screen that described the weighting differently would be a second, unreviewed account of the matching method.
The star control's own label, naming the multiplier the scoring model applies.

entries.text: Answer {} real questions the current Parliament has voted on and see how your views compare with the parties' recorded votes.
entries.note: What the tool does, on the first screen. The placeholder is the question count. Registered because it states what the comparison IS — the parties' recorded votes, not an opinion of them.

entries.text: Answer {} real questions parliament has voted on and see how your views compare with the parties' recorded votes, for your {} ballot — House and Senate.
entries.note: The same claim for an election that has a ballot. Placeholders are the question count and the election year.

entries.text: The next federal election hasn't been announced yet, so this is a provisional comparison against the current Parliament — the questions may change, and there are no candidates or printable how-to-vote plan yet.
entries.note: Bounds what a provisional comparison is and is not, before a voter starts one. Without it the first screen would imply a comparison against an election that has not been called.

entries.text: This election has already been held — what follows is a historical comparison, scored on the record as it stood then.
entries.note: Marks a past election as historical, so a comparison against it is not mistaken for current advice.

entries.text: Built from real parliamentary voting records
entries.note: A claim about the basis of the comparison, made on the first screen.

entries.text: Even-handed — the method is public and deterministic
entries.note: A neutrality claim, and one the methodology page has to keep true.

entries.text: No account, works offline, analytics off by default
entries.note: A privacy claim: no account, on-device, analytics off unless chosen. Registered so the native surface cannot state a weaker or stronger version of it than the web.
